newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Daewoo Bulgaria dismantles cars for export to CIS.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo Bulgaria dismantles cars for export to CIS.

text.p: The Bulgarian subsidiary of South Korea's giant Daewoo Corp has begun exporting thousands of disassembled Daewoo cars from Bulgaria to Russia and other former Soviet republics, officials said on Monday.

"Some 3,000 Daewoo cars have been shipped to the Bulgarian Black Sea ports of Varna and Bourgas where they are being disassembled and exported to former Soviet republics where they are being assembled again," a company official told Reuters.
Another company official said Daewoo Bulgaria was seeking to establish a long-term operation that would involve tens of thousands of Daewoo cars.
The official said the disassembled cars were shipped to former Soviet Black Sea ports, said the official but declined to provide further details.
Customs duties levied on car parts are lower than on fully assembled cars.
The South Korean conglomerate launched its subsidiary in Bulgaria last year in a move to step up its activities in this crisis-ridden Balkan country.
Daewoo has shown interest in investing in Bulgarian banks, chemical industry, telecommunications, machine building and tourism.
Daewoo Corp established a branch in Bulgaria in 1992. Last month, it bought a 67 percent stake in the Sheraton Sofia Hotel Balkan and pledged to invest some $5 million in it over the next five years.

A year ago, a car-making joint venture between Rover Group Ltd, a subsidiary of German automaker Bayerische Motoren Werke AG, and a Bulgarian consortium, closed down citing bureaucratic obstacles and lack of government support.
